newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The German central bank left the nation's two key interest rates unchanged at its regular meeting Thursday.
The Bundesbank, as expected, left the discount rate, the floor on interest rates, at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate, the ceiling on rates, at 4.50 percent.
The central bank also kept its main money market rate, the repo, steady at a fixed rate of 3 percent.
Economists said calm on the currency markets meant the Bundesbank had no need to defend the German mark by echoing last week's rise in U.S. interest rates.
All 10 economists surveyed by Reuters had expected the Bundesbank to leave interest rates unchanged at the meeting.
Signs that the German economy may be starting to recover hold little immediate threat of a change in interest rates, analysts said.
They argue that while inflation remained low, even though unemployment was at record post-war highs, there was little chance for either a rate cut or a rate hike.
